title: api: schema-versioning - add beta headers, deprecations, and backward-compat shims for response shape
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: We are introducing a light-weight API schema-versioning mechanism to allow incremental rollout of structured output and tool-calling response shape changes while preserving compatibility with existing OpenAI-compatible clients. This PR adds a beta header mechanism, deprecation metadata in responses, and runtime backward-compatibility shims that map new fields back to legacy shapes when requested. The goal is to reduce breakage for external integrators while allowing us to iterate on structured-output and tool-calling semantics.

What this PR does (high-level):
- Adds support for Accept-Redwood-Version and Accept-Redwood-Beta request headers to opt-in to schema versions and beta feature toggles.
- Introduces response-level deprecation metadata (response.deprecation_reason and response.deprecated_fields) for consumers to detect upcoming removals.
- Implements backward-compatibility shims in the OpenAI compatibility layer: when client does not opt into a new schema version, server synthesizes legacy fields (e.g., choices[].text, choices[].finish_reason) from the new structured output/segments representation.
- Streaming stability: standardizes intermediate SSE events for structured-output chunks and EOS markers; improves partial token handling so downstream stream parsers (OpenAI-compatible) don't see truncated JSON blobs. Adds defensive buffering and explicit boundary events.
- Adds migration documentation and a deprecation timeline: 3 months notice window for next major shape removal; tooling to detect usage of deprecated fields in production via the Console.

Key design notes:
- Versioning model: semantic-ish version token strings (e.g., "sov1", "sov1.1"). Default behavior remains backward-compatible (no header = best-effort compatibility). Explicit header values opt the request into the corresponding schema. Beta headers (Accept-Redwood-Beta: structured-output-v2) allow safe experimentation.
- Shims are best-effort and lossy in some edge cases (multi-tool-calls collapsed into choices[].text); we log shim activations as an event so we can monitor coverage and move clients to modern schema.
- OpenAI compatibility layer now supports both legacy completions/chat shapes and the newer structured tool-calling JSON blobs; translation occurs at the API boundary.

Checklist:
- [x] Add request header parsing and validation
- [x] Add response deprecation metadata and telemetry hooks
- [x] Implement shim translation code paths and unit tests
- [x] Update streaming SSE framing and add end-of-response markers
- [x] Update doc pages + migration guide + SDK compatibility notes
- [x] Add feature flag gating and rollout plan

Files changed (high level):
- server/api/headers.go: parse Accept-Redwood-Version / Accept-Redwood-Beta and expose on request context
- server/api/versioning.go: version negotiation and schema registry helper methods
- server/compat/openai/translate.go: new shim functions translating structured-output -> legacy choices/texts (largest file)
- server/compat/openai/streaming.go: stabilized SSE framing, explicit chunk types (partial_struct, partial_text, eos)
- docs/api/versioning.md: migration guide and deprecation timeline
- docs/openai-compat.md: notes about translation caveats and examples
- console/telemetry/rules.yaml: telemetry rules to flag shim usage and deprecated-field access
- tests/*: unit + integration tests for header negotiation, shim correctness, streaming stability

Commits summary: ["feat(api): add Accept-Redwood-Version and Accept-Redwood-Beta header parsing", "feat(compat): implement structured-output -> legacy shim translations", "fix(streaming): stabilize SSE framing and add explicit EOS events", "docs: add versioning + migration guide and openai-compat caveats", "test: add end-to-end tests for schema negotiation and fallback behavior"]

CI notes: All checks passing on merge. There was a transient flaky test (streaming_parser_test) on initial run; reran and it passed. Strongly recommend monitoring the new telemetry rule for shim activations for first 48 hours after rollout.

Rollout plan: Canary on Dedicated region eu-west-1 for 24h with telemetry alerts, then gradual rollout to hosted API. Beta headers default off; SDKs will opt-in in the next minor release. Deprecation timeline is documented in docs/api/versioning.md (3 months notice for removing deprecated fields).

Backwards-compat considerations and limitations: The shim preserves core behaviour for most chat/completion callers but cannot fully reconstruct complex structured tool-calling results (multiple tool calls with nested outputs) into a single choices[].text without lossy joins — in those cases we flatten and add a shim-warning field to the metadata. Customers with strict parsing should opt into the newer schema via the header.

Related: ENG-4821, PM-9102, SUP-1227. References to previous PRs/doctrine: pr-48231-api-schema-versioning-deprecations-beta-headers-backcompat-shims.json (prior iteration), and openai-compat updates in pr-51789.
